findings.recommendation: `Account` is a type of the public HTTP API (src/api.rs:1), so every existing client that reads `user_name` from the account response gets a missing field after deploy, with no warning. Mark the rename **BREAKING** in the release note (it is only listed as "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase.") with what clients must do, and give consumers a transition: emit both `user_name` and `userName` for a deprecation period (e.g. a second serialized field or a versioned endpoint), then remove `user_name` in a later release.
findings.title: Public JSON field renamed with no BREAKING mark nor compatibility path

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running 0005 on production permanently deletes every `users.legacy_email` value imported in 2023 ("not written since" does not mean empty), and there is no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql`, while 0004 ships one (`migrations/0004_accounts.down.sql`). Add a down migration that re-adds the nullable column, and a backup step before the drop (e.g. copy `id, legacy_email` into an archive table or export it), or state in the plan why the data can be lost and how to recover it.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration nor backup
